question: During meiosis, a cell divides to create ______ new cells.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Four**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• During meiosis, a single cell divides twice to produce four cells.
 
• These four cells are called gametes, which are sperm in males and eggs in females.
 
• Each of these gametes contains half the number of chromosomes of the original cell.
 
• This reduction in chromosome number is crucial for maintaining the species' chromosome number across generations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Phases of Meiosis:**

 
 
• Meiosis consists of two stages: Meiosis I and Meiosis II.
 
• Meiosis I includes Prophase I, Metaphase I, Anaphase I, and Telophase I.
 
• Meiosis II includes Prophase II, Metaphase II, Anaphase II, and Telophase II.
 
 
 
• **Genetic Diversity:**
 
 
• Meiosis increases genetic diversity through processes like crossing over and independent assortment.
 
• Crossing over occurs during Prophase I, where homologous chromosomes exchange genetic material.
 
 
 
• **Chromosome Number:**
 
 
• Humans have 46 chromosomes, which are reduced to 23 chromosomes in gametes through meiosis.
 
• When fertilization occurs, the chromosome number is restored to 46 in the zygote.
 
 
 
• **Errors in Meiosis:**
 
 
• Errors during meiosis can lead to genetic disorders such as Down syndrome, which is caused by an extra copy of chromosome 21.
 
• These errors are often due to nondisjunction, where chromosomes fail to separate properly.
